title: Strategies to Mitigate Risk Factors Implementing Building Information Modelling: A Multi-Dimensional Perspective
content: Building Information Modelling (BIM) has attracted considerable attention in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry owing to its inherent advantages such as enhancing construction design and process. However, the integration of BIM presents risks that are often overlooked in project implementations without mitigating strategies (management strategies) that this study fulfils. This study encompasses an in-depth analysis of BIM and other IT—related studies through an integrative review approach, scrutinising distinct knowledge domains—BIM implementation and risk management process, focusing on risk breakdown structure (RBS) and management strategies. This study utilises an exploratory-based review centred around journal articles and conference papers sourced from Scopus and Google Scholar between 2000 and 2024. Initial data collection involved triangulating key search terms on these platforms, which were then processed using NVivo 12 Pro software to categorise risks through thematic analysis, resulting in a comprehensive Risk Breakdown Structure (RBS). Qualitative analysis was employed to identify management strategies, subsequently illuminating the specific connections between these strategies and the risks involved. The findings accentuate the crucial linkages of key strategies such as implementing Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) standard data schema to mitigate interoperability issues and employing Fuzzy analysis to minimise cultural barriers were identified. The study establishes a valuable critical review and knowledge repository for construction industry stakeholders. Importantly, extending into underexplored domains, particularly risk management strategies across the techno-organisational and socio-organisational spectrum. This research contributes to bridging the existing research gap in understanding the intricate relationship between BIM implementation risks and effective management strategies within the AEC industry. The practical implications of this study are profound with global relevance because the novel developed multi-dimensional framework can serve as a knowledge base that can be adapted and adopted by both academic and industry professionals.
